# Copilot Instructions for ExcelJS

## Project Overview

ExcelJS is a Node.js library for reading and writing Excel (XLSX) and CSV spreadsheet files. It supports rich formatting, formulas, streaming I/O, images, charts, pivot tables, and TypeScript type definitions. The library also ships a browser-compatible bundle.

- **Entry point (Node.js):** `excel.js` → `lib/exceljs.nodejs.js`
- **Entry point (browser):** `dist/exceljs.min.js` (generated by build)
- **TypeScript types:** `index.d.ts` / `index.ts`
- **Package manager:** Yarn (Berry / v4, `nodeLinker: node-modules`; version pinned via `packageManager` + Corepack)
- **Build system:** esbuild (`scripts/build.js`) — emits the browser UMD bundles in `dist/` and the CommonJS build in `dist/cjs/`
- **Test framework:** Mocha + Chai (`spec/`); browser tests run in headless Chromium via Playwright (`scripts/test-browser.js`)
- **Linter:** ESLint flat config (`eslint.config.js`) — a curated strict rule set (`@eslint/js` recommended + `eslint-plugin-n` + `eslint-plugin-import-x`); formatting is owned by Prettier (`.prettierrc`), wired in via `eslint-config-prettier`

## Repository Layout

```
lib/
  doc/          # Core document model: Workbook, Worksheet, Row, Column, Cell, etc.
  xlsx/         # XLSX read/write engine
    xform/      # XML transformer classes (one per XLSX element)
  csv/          # CSV read/write support
  stream/       # Streaming workbook reader/writer
  utils/        # Shared utilities (col-cache, xml-stream, shared-strings, etc.)
scripts/
  build.js      # esbuild build (browser bundles + dist/cjs); shims/ for browser polyfills
  test-browser.js  # Playwright headless-Chromium browser test runner
spec/
  unit/         # Unit tests (fast, no I/O)
  integration/  # Integration tests (read/write real files)
  end-to-end/   # End-to-end tests (includes Express server test)
  dist/         # Tests that exercise the built bundles
  typescript/   # TypeScript type compatibility tests
  config/       # Mocha setup helpers (setup.js, setup-unit.js)
  utils/        # verquire helper – switches between the source and the built code
dist/           # Generated bundles + dist/cjs (not committed; created by `yarn build`)
index.d.ts      # Public TypeScript type definitions
```

## Development Workflow

### Install dependencies

```bash
corepack enable   # once, to activate the pinned Yarn version
yarn install
```

### Build (required before running the full test suite or browser tests)

```bash
yarn build
```

This runs `node scripts/build.js`, which uses esbuild to:

1. Bundle the browser UMD builds `dist/exceljs.js` / `dist/exceljs.min.js` (plus `.bare` variants)
2. Emit the CommonJS build under `dist/cjs/`

### Lint & format

```bash
yarn lint          # ESLint — correctness & code quality
yarn lint:fix      # eslint . --fix
yarn format        # prettier --write .   (formatting is owned by Prettier)
```

### Run tests

| Command                 | What it runs                                                       |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `yarn test:unit`        | Unit tests only (fast, no build needed)                            |
| `yarn test:integration` | Integration tests                                                  |
| `yarn test:end-to-end`  | End-to-end tests                                                   |
| `yarn test:browser`     | Browser tests (builds, then runs headless Chromium via Playwright) |
| `yarn test:typescript`  | TypeScript type-checking tests                                     |
| `yarn test:full`        | Build + unit + integration + end-to-end + browser                  |
| `yarn test`             | Alias for `test:full`                                              |

For most feature/bug work the fastest meaningful cycle is:

```bash
yarn test:unit && yarn test:integration
```

### Benchmark

```bash
yarn benchmark
```

## Code Style and Conventions

- **ESLint config:** curated strict flat config in `eslint.config.js` — `@eslint/js` recommended + `eslint-plugin-n` + `eslint-plugin-import-x`, with `eslint-config-prettier` last so ESLint defers all formatting to Prettier
- **Prettier config:** single quotes, 2-space indent, no semicolons, trailing commas (see `.prettierrc`)
- Single quotes for strings, semicolons required, max line length 120 chars (comments/strings exempt)
- `n/no-unsupported-features/es-syntax` targets Node >=10
- No `for...in` loops (`no-restricted-syntax`); use `for...of` or array methods
- Use `verquire(path)` instead of `require(path)` in test files so tests can run against either the source `lib/` build or the compiled CommonJS `dist/cjs/` build

## Key Architectural Patterns

### Document Model (`lib/doc/`)

The public API surface. `Workbook` owns an array of `Worksheet` objects; each worksheet owns `Row` and `Column` objects; each row owns `Cell` objects. Model objects expose a plain `.model` property (a plain JS object) that is the canonical serialization format described in `MODEL.md`.

### XFORM Pattern (`lib/xlsx/xform/`)

Each class in this directory is an XML transformer responsible for reading or writing one XLSX XML element. They follow a consistent interface:

- `render(xmlStream, model)` – serialize a model to XML
- `parseOpen(node)` / `parseText(text)` / `parseClose(tag)` – SAX-style parse callbacks
- `reconcile(model, context)` – post-parse reconciliation pass

When adding support for a new XLSX feature, create or extend the appropriate xform class.

### Streaming API (`lib/stream/`)

`stream/xlsx/workbook-writer.js` and `stream/xlsx/workbook-reader.js` provide memory-efficient streaming variants. Changes to the streaming API should be mirrored in the document API where applicable.

### TypeScript Definitions (`index.d.ts`)

All public API changes must be reflected here. TypeScript tests live in `spec/typescript/`.

## Making Changes

### Adding a feature or fixing a bug

1. Make changes in `lib/` (document model and/or xform layer)
2. Update `index.d.ts` if the public API changes
3. Add or update tests in `spec/unit/` and/or `spec/integration/`
4. Run `yarn lint` and fix any issues
5. Run `yarn test:unit && yarn test:integration` to verify

### Changing XLSX read/write behaviour

- Edit the relevant xform in `lib/xlsx/xform/`
- Add a fixture or expected output in `spec/integration/data/` or `spec/unit/xlsx/xform/`
- Run integration tests: `yarn test:integration`

### Updating TypeScript types only

- Edit `index.d.ts`
- Run `yarn test:typescript` (uses `ts-node`)

## Known Issues and Workarounds

- **Full test suite requires a build first.** Running `yarn test` calls `yarn build` internally. If you only want to run unit tests without building, use `yarn test:unit` directly.
- **Browser tests need Chromium.** `yarn test:browser` runs the bundles in headless Chromium via Playwright; run `yarn playwright install chromium` once so the browser is available.
- **`verquire` in tests.** Test files must use `verquire('path/relative/to/lib')` instead of `require` so they work against both the source (`lib/`) and the compiled CommonJS (`dist/cjs/`) build. The build is selected via the `EXCEL_BUILD=cjs` environment variable; importing directly via `require('../../lib/...')` will break the built-code test runs.
- **`dist/` is generated.** Never edit files in `dist/` directly; they are overwritten by `yarn build`.
- **Windows line endings.** The CI workflow sets `core.autocrlf false` for Windows. If working on Windows, keep the same git config to avoid diff noise.
